leaves.text: What were net sales in FY2021, FY2024 and FY2025, and the compound annual growth rate from FY2021 to FY2025?
leaves.answer: $488.1m in FY2021, $590.6m in FY2024 and $620.0m in FY2025: 6.2% a year from FY2021. FY2025 and FY2024 are the model's starting revenue.

leaves.text: How much did net sales grow in FY2025, and how much of the change came from volume, price and currency?
leaves.answer: 4.98%, or $29.4m. Volume added about $25.2m, price about $5.6m and currency translation took off $1.4m.

leaves.text: What growth did management guide for FY2026, from what base and at what exchange rates?
leaves.answer: 5%-9% from FY2025 pro forma results, which exclude the Americas homecare and cleaning brands held for sale, at FY2025 average exchange rates: $630-655m.

leaves.text: How much FY2025 revenue does the guidance base leave out, and does the release say what the excluded brands sell?
leaves.answer: The guidance starts from currency-adjusted pro forma FY2025 net sales of about $603m, against $620.0m reported, so about $17.0m sits outside the base. The release does not split that amount, so it only bounds the excluded brands' FY2025 sales from above. The release's $12.5m is a different figure: how much higher FY2026 net sales guidance would be if the sale did not happen. The scenarios grow reported revenue and assume no sale proceeds. Taking the whole $17.0m out of the Americas would change Base growth in years 2-5 by 0.05 points.

laterInformation.text: In July 2026 the company moved the brands from held for sale back to held for use and put their contribution at about $12m of net sales and $2.9m of operating income.

leaves.text: Which growth rates do the scenarios use, and how do they compare with the FY2021-FY2025 rate?
leaves.answer: Year 1 is set at the guidance range on the reported base: Bear 1.62%, Base 3.63%, Bull 5.65%. Years 2-5 come from a regional build (Americas/EIMEA/Asia-Pacific: Bear 2/4/5%, Base 4/7/8%, Bull 6/9/11%; analyst assumptions), compressed to one rate: Bear 3.25%, Base 5.81%, Bull 7.98% a year, against 6.2% in FY2021-FY2025.

leaves.answer: Open at the case date.

leaves.text: What was the gross margin in each fiscal year from 2021 to 2025?
What explained the change in gross margin from FY2024 to FY2025?
leaves.answer: The filing names lower specialty chemical costs (+80 bp), lower aerosol can costs (+60 bp) and higher average selling prices (+50 bp), less higher warehousing, distribution and freight costs (-50 bp). Gross margin rose 168 bp; the named drivers add up to 140 bp, leaving about 28 bp that the filing does not attribute.

leaves.text: What was the reported operating margin in each fiscal year from 2021 to 2025?
leaves.answer: FY2021 18.2%, FY2022 16.8%, FY2023 16.7%, FY2024 16.3%, FY2025 16.7%. FY2025 is $103.793m over $619.985m, before the workbook's R&D adjustment.

leaves.text: How does the workbook's R&D capitalization change FY2025 operating income?
leaves.answer: It adds back FY2025 R&D of $8.7m and subtracts a third of each of the three prior years' R&D ($8.0m, $6.2m and $5.1m), $6.43m in total. Operating income rises by $2.27m to $106.06m, a 17.11% margin against 16.74% reported. The three-year life is an analyst assumption; the company expenses R&D.

leaves.text: How far was FY2025 cost of doing business from the company's own target?
leaves.answer: 37% of net sales against a long-term target of 30%; gross margin was at its 55% target and adjusted EBITDA was 18% against 25%.

leaves.text: Which margin paths do the scenarios use, and on what basis?
leaves.answer: Year-1 margins come from operating-income guidance plus the workbook's R&D adjustment: Bear 16.7%, Base 16.9%, Bull 17.1%. By year 5: Bear stays at its year-1 margin, Base 18%, Bull 20%. FY2017-FY2020 averaged 19.4% reported. The company's long-term model targets adjusted EBITDA of 25%, not an operating margin, so no filing gives the 18% or 20% directly: both are analyst assumptions.

No filing establishes a permanent excess return; the Base and Bull figures rest on the brand and the low capital needs above, and are analyst assumptions.

leaves.text: What reinvestment does each case's terminal growth and return on new capital imply?
leaves.answer: Reinvestment is growth over the return on new capital: Original 2.5% / 8.00% = 31.2%; Bear 2.0% / 9.45% = 21.2%; Base 2.5% / 15.00% = 16.7%; Bull 3.0% / 20.00% = 15.0% of after-tax operating income. A higher assumed return lets the same growth come with less reinvestment, so the two have to be read together.

leaves.text: What share of operating value comes from after year 10 in each case?
leaves.answer: Original 55%; Bear 47%; Base 64%; Bull 75%. The cases with higher growth and returns lean more on the years after the forecast.

leaves.answer: From $94.636m to $86.995m. With cash of $58.130m, borrowings net of cash were $28.865m at FY2025 year-end; the DCF subtracts the debt and adds the cash.

leaves.text: With the Base financing terms, what is the highest price per share a buyer can pay and still earn its target return?
leaves.answer: $74.87 (boundary found), an entry multiple of 9.4 times EBITDA. Terms: 5.0 times FY2025 EBITDA of debt at SOFR on 29 Aug 2025 plus 3.5% (7.84%), a 20% target return, and an exit after five years at 11.2 times EBITDA, the peer median. Debt is repaid 1% a year, then from cash above a $30m minimum; fees are 2% on the transaction, 2.5% on the financing and 2% on exit. Counting the liability as debt would also require moving rent out of operating income.

topics.adaptation: FinCausal extracts cause and effect from financial text; FinanceBench asks for restructuring costs. The WD-40 version asks which costs move margins, through what channel, and which published figure would test the margin paths.

leaves.text: Which inputs does WD-40 name as its main costs, and how does the price of oil reach them?
leaves.answer: Specialty chemicals and aerosol cans. The 10-K says oil price volatility indirectly affects specialty chemical costs, many of which are indexed to refined oil products.

leaves.text: How did currency translation affect FY2025 net sales by segment?
leaves.answer: Americas -$4.7m, EIMEA +$3.5m, Asia-Pacific -$0.2m: -$1.4m in total.

leaves.text: Are restructuring costs shown separately in the FY2025 income statement?
leaves.answer: No restructuring line or restructuring fact appears in the FY2025 XBRL data, so the FinanceBench rule gives 0.

leaves.text: Will the FY2026 gross margin stay within the guided 55.5%-56.5% range?
leaves.answer: Open at the case date.

resolution.rule: Compare FY2026 gross margin on the original guidance perimeter (without the brands then held for sale) with the range. A margin below it would contradict the Base and Bull paths, which raise operating margin to 18% and 20%.
resolution.linkedAssumption: Input sheet!B27 and B29 (Base 16.9% and 18% operating margin)

laterInformation.text: The FY2026 10-K reports a gross margin of 55.3% ($380.5m over $688.0m), below the range but on a changed perimeter. In July 2026 the company moved the homecare brands back into the business and lowered its gross margin guidance to 54.5%-55.5%, putting 40 bp of the cut on that move and 60 bp on higher costs. The reported figure therefore does not resolve the question on the original basis.

FinLFQA.why: Records were chosen by their question text: the dataset's topic labels often do not match it, and no validation question asks about the cost of capital.

FinCausal.why: Cause-effect pairs from news about other companies; two shape the form of the disposal and oil-cost questions, and no figure from them enters an answer.

FinTextQA.why: The public part is 240 questions on banking regulation (Federal Reserve, HKMA, EU). None applies to a non-bank consumer products company; the textbook part was not released.
